question: are context tokens stable within a condition across repeats
design: one burned pilot task, two conditions, three repeats each, identical workspace digest within each condition, same pinned backend

falsifier_outcome.falsifier: if context tokens for the same condition and task vary widely across repeats, a per-episode report is not enough and cost must be modelled with repeats
falsifier_outcome.detail: the minimal condition varied by 2.90 percent, but the retrieval condition varied by 11.34 percent and its within-condition range of 17,231 tokens is 61.1 percent of the between-condition gap

mechanism_hypothesis: with dynamic retrieval the agent chooses how much of the evidence pack to read, so context cost is partly an outcome of agent behaviour rather than a fixed property of the condition; this is a hypothesis consistent with the four-fold larger spread, not a tested mechanism
attribution_limit: the two conditions differ in both factors at once, so nothing here attributes cost or its variance to retrieval or to the scaffold separately
claim_scope: cost instrument evidence only; no treatment effect is claimed
